text:
lia: quick design drop 
 two options for the streaming control: A) Separate buttons: [Stop] [Regenerate] B) Single toggle that becomes [Retry] after stop. screenshots attached. thoughts?

kevin: A. separate buttons make intent explicit. avoids accidental regen when hitting stop.

maria: A too. question: post-Stop do we keep partial text editable or clear it? affects edit+rerun flows.

lia: keep partial text in the chat and let user edit. Stop = interrupt; Regenerate = new run unless edited.

jon: token counter note: updating on every chunk is flickery. propose "sent / limit" display (e.g. 312 / 8192) and throttle UI updates + animate delta to feel smooth.

tasha: infra prefers throttling. 200ms UI throttle + emit telemetry at chunk boundaries only. reduces event QPS.

lia: a11y nit: icon-only label "Stop" might be ambiguous to SR. add aria-label="Stop generation" and tooltip "Esc to stop".

kevin: agree. keep visible text short but use aria-labels. also consider aria-live="polite" + aria-atomic="false" for streaming container to avoid SRs reading every chunk.

maria: prompt drawer behavior? push vs overlay. push keeps context (token meter visible), overlay is quicker. my vote: push on desktop, overlay on mobile.

jon: pushing needs careful scroll anchoring during streams. engineering: OK if we maintain pinned-bottom while stream is active.

lia: decision: run two-week A/B (A=Separate buttons, B=Compact toggle->Retry). Both variants use 200ms token throttle, aria-live markup, aria-labels and tooltip. capture events: ui.variant, action=stop|regen, stop_ms.

deploy-bot: FYI: streaming client deploy to staging scheduled Tue 09:00 PDT, will include experimental flag for ab_test_stream_controls.

lia: cool 
 I'll file the experiment ticket with mocks, a11y checklist, and acceptance criteria. :white_check_mark:
